title: Piaget held that young infants forget a toy once it is hidden
summary: OpenStax says that, in Piaget's view, young infants do not remember an object after it has been removed from sight.
body: OpenStax Psychology states Piaget's view directly: young infants do not remember an object after it has been removed from sight. That claim is why he treated the early months as coming before the hidden-object understanding. The sentence is the textbook's report of Piaget. It is not OpenStax's last word, and it is not a camera study. That is his claim in the textbook and not the textbook's last word on the topic.

sources.title: OpenStax Psychology, 9.2 Lifespan Theories
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Psychology web page, CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase; credit OpenStax. Supports Piaget's claim, as the textbook states it, that young infants do not remember an object removed from sight.
